cells.document: Formula of Concord, Epitome (Book of Concord)
cells.section: Article II, Free Will, Affirmative Theses 3 (par. 5-6)
cells.excerpt: are thus converted alone through the grace and power of the Holy Ghost, whose work alone the conversion of man is.
cells.shows: Conversion is taught as the work of the Holy Spirit alone, working through the Word, with no contribution from the unregenerate will.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (the monergist side of 33; read with the Article XI cell, which explains why the coordinate is not at the pole)

cells.document: Formula of Concord, Epitome (Book of Concord)
cells.excerpt: does not mean that God is not willing to save everybody; but the reason is that they either do not at all hear God's Word, but wilfully despise it
cells.shows: God's will to save is taught as universal and the Word can be wilfully despised, so that those who perish are themselves responsible and not God's election.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (this is the resistible-grace, universal-grace element that keeps the audited coordinate at 33, monergist-leaning, rather than at the monergist pole)

cells.section: Article X, Of the Lord's Supper
cells.excerpt: the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present, and are distributed to those who eat the Supper of the Lord; and they reject those that teach otherwise.
cells.shows: The body and blood of Christ are confessed as truly present and distributed in the Supper, and the contrary teaching is rejected.

cells.document: The Charismatic Movement and Lutheran Theology, report of the Commission on Theology and Church Relations, Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod
cells.section: Part II, analysis of the biblical data on spiritual gifts (discussion of 1 Corinthians 13)
cells.excerpt: nowhere promises or encourages us to hope that extraordinary charismatic gifts will become the possession of the Christian church
cells.shows: The report says Scripture gives no promise that the extraordinary gifts continue through the centuries and that the biblical pattern may indicate the opposite, while also saying 1 Corinthians 13 does not prove they ended with the apostles.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (a cautious, leaning cessationism, which fits 82 rather than the pole)

cells.section: Article XVII, Of Christ's Return to Judgment (par. 5)
cells.excerpt: that before the resurrection of the dead the godly shall take possession of the kingdom of the world, the ungodly being everywhere suppressed.
cells.shows: The confession condemns the opinion that the godly will hold an earthly kingdom before the resurrection of the dead, which excludes a millennial earthly reign.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports, but weaker than the coordinate on the Israel-and-church question itself: it rejects an earthly millennium and does not address a distinct future for national Israel (see the Brief Statement cell)

cells.document: A Brief Statement of the Doctrinal Position of the Missouri Synod
cells.excerpt: there will be no general conversion, a conversion en masse, of the Jewish nation
cells.shows: The Missouri Synod's statement rejects the whole of millennialism and denies a future mass conversion of the Jewish nation.

cells.document: Formula of Concord, Epitome (Book of Concord)
cells.section: Summary Content, Rule and Standard, par. 1
cells.excerpt: the sole rule and standard according to which all dogmas together with [all] teachers should be estimated and judged are the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures
cells.shows: Scripture alone is named as the only rule and standard by which all doctrines and teachers are judged; the same section treats creeds and other writings as witnesses, not judges.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (the retained creeds and confessions as subordinate witnesses fit 88 rather than the pole)

cells.excerpt: the Mass is retained among us, and celebrated with the highest reverence. Nearly all the usual ceremonies are also preserved
cells.shows: The confession states that the historic Mass and nearly all its customary ceremonies were kept in the Lutheran churches.

cells.document: Formula of Concord, Epitome (Book of Concord)
cells.section: Article X, Church Rites (Adiaphora), Affirmative Theses 2 (par. 4)
cells.excerpt: the congregation of God of every place and every time has the power, according to its circumstances, to change such ceremonies
cells.shows: Ceremonies neither commanded nor forbidden by God are held to be changeable by each church, so the liturgy is kept as good order and not as divine law.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (explains why the coordinate is 10 and not 0: liturgical in practice, free in principle)

notes: Every excerpt was copied from the page at the given URL, opened on 2026-09-19; the raw HTML of bookofconcord.org and projectwittenberg.org was downloaded and the sentences extracted by text search, not quoted from memory. On bookofconcord.org the running text carries inline paragraph numbers (for example 'distributed 2 to those'); these were removed from the excerpts and nothing else was altered; the page's HTML apostrophe entity in 'God's Word' was rendered as a plain apostrophe. The bookofconcord.org text is the Bente/Dau Triglotta English (1921, public domain). Dates of 1530 and 1577/1580 are the standard dates of the Augsburg Confession and the Formula of Concord; the pages opened do not themselves print a date. The Book of Concord is binding on confessional Lutheran bodies (LCMS, WELS, ELS and others) by subscription. The Book of Concord has no article on the cessation of miraculous gifts, so the gifts cell uses a Missouri Synod commission report: it is representative of one confessional body, was not adopted as binding doctrine, and is in copyright (link only). The 1932 Brief Statement is an adopted doctrinal statement of the Missouri Synod only, not of all confessional Lutherans, so it is marked not binding for the tradition as a whole, and link only because its copyright status was not checked. The official LCMS page for the Brief Statement (https://www.lcms.org/about/beliefs/doctrine/brief-statement-of-lcms-doctrinal-position) was opened but the fetched text was truncated before par. 42, so the Project Wittenberg copy is the one cited. The kingdom axis is the weakest fit: the confessions reject an earthly millennium but say nothing directly about Israel and the church as one people; no confessional text was found that states that in so many words. No cell points against the audited coordinates.
